negative_findings.description: No standalone, group-published Kosovo card/POS/ATM statistical dataset was found for any parent group — Kosovo card, terminal and digital-channel numbers appear only embedded in narrative sections of annual reports/presentations, never as a downloadable data series.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches across RBI, ProCredit Holding, NLB, TEB, Ziraat and BKT returned only PDF reports and presentations; no data portal, XLS annex or API surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for A4 payment/card statistics from group sources must be PDF-extraction based, with manual QA; automated tabular ingestion is not available.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language (sr) searching produced no group-level Kosovo banking disclosures beyond NLB's own English/Slovene material.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'NLB grupa godišnji izveštaj Kosovo banka tržišni udeo kartice' returned only NLB group English pages, Wikipedia entries and NLB Montenegro reports — no Serbian-language parent-group publication covering Kosovo card/terminal statistics.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For this cell, sr is a low-yield language: the relevant parent groups publish in en, de, sl, tr and sq. Effort should be redirected accordingly, but this must be recorded rather than assumed.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo-specific disclosure was located at the BNP Paribas group level (as opposed to TEB A.Ş. / TEB Kosovo level).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced TEB Kosovo and TEB Türkiye reports but nothing where BNP Paribas group reporting breaks out Kosovo; BNP's link is indirect via the TEB joint venture (BNP Paribas Fortis Yatırımlar Holding).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts should not expect Kosovo lines in BNP Paribas universal registration documents; the TEB chain is the usable disclosure path.

negative_findings.description: Several hub URLs in this slice were inferred from publisher structure or cited inside search results rather than returned as direct hits (ProCredit Holding IR hub, ziraatbank-kosova.com, kap.org.tr English path).
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence scores and flagged here; no fetch was performed, so nothing is asserted about liveness.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass should treat these as priority checks; failures are likely path changes, not dead publishers.

coverage_gaps.description: Cell scope named six parent groups, but Kosovo also hosts foreign-owned banks/IFI-backed institutions outside the list (e.g. Turkish-owned Is Bank presence, IFI shareholders such as EBRD/IFC/KfW in ProCredit, and Albanian-owned non-bank payment players).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the actor map with IFI shareholder reporting (EBRD/IFC project documents on Kosovo banks) which often discloses card/digital-inclusion indicators not in commercial reports.

coverage_gaps.description: Credit rating agency reports and analyst notes on the parent groups (Moody's, Fitch, S&P) were not searched in this slice; they frequently contain subsidiary-level Kosovo commentary and peer market-share tables.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on rating-agency press releases and rating action reports for RBI, NLB, ProCredit and BKT that mention Kosovo.

coverage_gaps.description: German-language sources (ProCredit Holding is Frankfurt-listed; RBI is Vienna-listed) were not searched, although the run's language set is sq/sr/en.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add de-language queries (Geschäftsbericht, Länderbericht, Offenlegungsbericht, Bundesanzeiger filings) to reach the statutory German-language versions that sometimes carry fuller country annexes.

coverage_gaps.description: Back-series depth is uncertain: current IR sites expose roughly the last 5-8 years, while older Kosovo subsidiary reports appear only on third-party mirrors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan an archive pass (Wayback Machine on raiffeisen-kosovo.com, nlb-kos.com, procreditbank-kos.com report indices) to reconstruct pre-2015 card/ATM/POS series.

coverage_gaps.description: Group disclosures give Kosovo P&L and portfolio lines reliably, but cash-usage indicators (ATM withdrawal volumes, cash-in/cash-out) were not found at group level for any parent.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat cash usage as a gap to be filled from Central Bank of Kosovo statistics and from ATM/self-service narrative in subsidiary reports; do not expect it from parent filings.

brief: Kosovo's majority foreign-owned banking market is documented far better abroad than at home: RBI (Vienna), ProCredit Holding (Frankfurt) and NLB (Ljubljana) all publish recurring, dated, country-level Kosovo figures — RBI via segment/country tables and CRD Art. 89 country-by-country disclosure, ProCredit via a per-country key-figures table, NLB via quarterly results decks with Kosovo market share and digital-channel KPIs. The Turkish/Albanian chain (TEB A.S. and KAP filings; Ziraat's integrated report; BKT Albania and Calik Holding) is thinner and narrative rather than tabular, but is the only public window on two significant card-issuing and acquiring banks. Card, ATM/POS and digital-channel detail is concentrated not in the parent filings but in the group-template subsidiary annual reports (Raiffeisen Kosovo, NLB Prishtina, ProCredit Kosovo, TEB Kosovo), which should be the collection backbone, with parent filings used for comparability and validation. Everything found is PDF/HTML narrative — no group-level Kosovo data feed exists, and cash-usage indicators are absent from group sources entirely.
